author: Travis Chinn
title: Boji Mammoths Hockey Club takes part in Hockey Fights Cancer - NewsBreak
text:
By Travis Chinn Maren Ewertz No media credit provided. ,
43 minutes ago
SPIRIT LAKE , Iowa ( KCAU ) — The Boji Mammoths have been around since 2016, and this year, they’re doing something they’ve never done before — participating in Hockey Fights Cancer .
“Boji Mammoths are our high school hockey team located in northwest Iowa, in Spirit Lake, but Boji Mammoths, we draw from all the area high schools; we have kids from Lake Park, from Estherville, Spirit Lake, and Okoboji,” said Daniel Hoerichs, Assistant Coach for the Boji Mammoths.
This season, the Boji Mammoths decided to participate in Hockey Fights Cancer.
“We were approached by a donor who was interested in purchasing jerseys for a Hockey Fights Cancer night. That we could show off and auction off, and we decided well, we should make it a whole event as well, not just wearing the jerseys for a game,” added Hoerichs.
Story continues below
Hockey Fights Cancer was started in 1998 as a joint venture between the National Hockey League and the National Hockey League Players Association.
The Mammoths are able to participate through ‘HFC Assist.’ HFC Assist allows junior and youth hockey clubs to support Hockey Fights Cancer.
“I’ve had a lot of people in my family affected by it. I think it’s a great awareness and great support for everyone that struggles with that. It affects everyone. No matter how big. How small. I think it’s great that we’re doing this,” said Cael Cornell, a junior from Spirit Lake.
“It’s a great cause. I have a lot of people in my family that struggle with cancer. My aunt just got re-diagnosed with skin cancer, so it means a lot that they’re having this event on Saturday,” said Karter Wulf, a junior from Spirit Lake.
The Mammoths Hockey Fights Cancer game is this Saturday, February 7, with a Junior Varsity game at 2:00 p.m. and a varsity game at 4:00 p.m., both against the Lincoln Junior Stars.
“There’s been a core group of people that have been helping to plan it and making it really special for our first one,” added Hoerichs.
The team will wear special jerseys that will be raffled off. There will also be a 50/50 raffle, free-will admission donations, and a tailgate at 3:00 p.m.
“See you on Saturday, pack the cave, make it an awesome event,” said Wulf. “Tailgate at 3:00 p.m. with Burger and Company before, so, yeah, make it awesome. Pack the cave.”
